subject.title: chore(agent): port audit guardrails to mainline

question: Should OpenClaw make execution packets a fail-closed requirement for existing `sessions_spawn` and cron `agentTurn` tool calls, or keep current calls compatible while introducing any stricter audit policy separately?
rationale: The proposed text-derived gate adds a new model-facing contract and can stop established delegated workflows; choosing its permanent default cannot be safely inferred from tests or contributor proof.

options.title: Preserve existing calls by default
options.body: Keep current delegated-task calls working and redesign any strict execution-packet requirement as an explicitly approved, documented migration or opt-in policy after the rebase.

options.title: Approve fail-closed packet enforcement
options.body: Adopt the new requirement only with a maintainer-owned compatibility statement, upgrade proof for existing tool callers, and explicit documentation of the failure mode.

options.title: Split the audit tooling
options.body: Land only independently useful guard tooling in a narrow rebased PR and leave the runtime policy proposal for a separate design discussion.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing calls by default
recommendation.body: Keep current delegated-task calls working and redesign any strict execution-packet requirement as an explicitly approved, documented migration or opt-in policy after the rebase.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the affected agent-tool path makes this the best available routing candidate for the behavior contract.
